boundaries.contract: Default MCP lifecycle, collector-failure, startup, and transport-failure logs use fixed text or bounded diagnostics and do not attach Request, Response, ResourceMethod, or Throwable carriers.
boundaries.name: Built-in fixed and redacted MCP logs

boundaries.contract: Trace-correlation records and unknown mirrored-header name diagnostics are absent by default; explicit configuration enables only their documented bounded or redacted fields, and raw validated trace IDs require a separate opt-in.
boundaries.name: Opt-in trace and unknown-header diagnostics

boundaries.contract: All built-in metric emissions use the sealed typed event vocabulary and finite endpoint, method, outcome, reason, code, duration, and count dimensions; Request, Throwable, trace, cursor, state, baggage, and arbitrary application data are not metric dimensions.
boundaries.name: Built-in MCP metric emissions

boundaries.contract: The generic LogEvent API deliberately permits an application or non-MCP Soklet path to attach an exact Request. Built-in MCP LogEvents do not use this attachment; applications own disclosure when constructing or rendering custom events.
boundaries.name: Generic LogEvent Request attachments

boundaries.contract: The generic LogEvent API deliberately permits exact Throwable attachment and preserves identity. Built-in MCP LogEvents omit Throwable attachments and the terminal fallback emits only the Throwable class; applications own custom-event rendering and retention.
boundaries.name: Generic LogEvent Throwable attachments

boundaries.contract: Request, trace, multipart, and application-facing MCP request/context carriers, their nested builders and transitive implementations, and callback signatures deliberately expose exact application values through documented accessors; applications own any logging, retention, or export.
boundaries.name: Application request/context carrier and callback exposure

boundaries.contract: Soklet-owned Request exception messages redact path, parameter, header, cookie, form, and multipart values. Existing structured exception accessors intentionally preserve exact values for application error handling, so applications own logging or disclosure of those accessors.
boundaries.name: Request exception message and structured-value split

boundaries.contract: The off-network simulator intentionally returns exact response headers, bodies, SSE bytes and messages, and terminal Throwable identities to its caller, under configured item and byte bounds. Simulator callers own fixture storage, logging, and disclosure.
boundaries.name: Local MCP simulator capture

boundaries.contract: Inventoried MCP request diagnostics and the default terminal reporter replace or cap exact application-controlled values before rendering; accessors that deliberately retain exact values are classified separately.
boundaries.name: Redacted MCP and terminal diagnostic renderers

boundaries.contract: Generic LogEvent rendering may include an application-supplied message or Throwable, result metadata preserves application extension values, and typed-schema paths preserve bounded escaped application property names. Callers own whether these exact diagnostic representations are logged or retained.
boundaries.name: Intentional exact application diagnostic renderers

boundaries.contract: Server, lifecycle, termination, and core-finalization diagnostics expose only finite status, counts, capped summaries, fingerprints, configuration flags, and other bounded metadata.
boundaries.name: Finite metadata-only server and lifecycle diagnostics

boundaries.contract: Application-created JSON-RPC errors, their public/internal carriers, exact accessors, conversion sites, and qualified constructions deliberately preserve application-supplied code, message, and structured data for wire publication.
boundaries.name: Application JSON-RPC error publication

boundaries.contract: Framework-owned parse, envelope, header, state, admission, overload, routing, capability, and internal errors use fixed or bounded messages and structured data. Raw handler Throwables, request carriers, authorization values, cursors, request state, and trace metadata are not serialized.
boundaries.name: Framework JSON-RPC error publication

boundaries.contract: Every tracked golden error-mapping wire artifact and manifest is explicitly inventoried; the corpus test proves checksum completeness and the fixed or bounded production error vocabulary.
boundaries.name: Golden error-mapping fixtures

boundaries.contract: Every tracked precedence/no-store HTTP wire artifact and manifest is explicitly inventoried and checksum-bound, including secret-canary failure paths whose published errors remain fixed.
boundaries.name: Golden HTTP contract fixtures

boundaries.contract: Every tracked authorization/CORS response-head fixture and manifest is explicitly inventoried; bearer values are inputs only and the stored heads contain only the reviewed challenge and CORS contract.
boundaries.name: Golden authorization and CORS heads

boundaries.contract: Every tracked complete/input-required JSON or SSE result fixture and manifest is explicitly inventoried and checksum-bound; framework failures use redacted errors while intentional application results remain exact fixture data.
boundaries.name: Golden result-envelope fixtures

boundaries.contract: Every tracked official phase 3, 4, and 5 golden-wire request/response artifact and manifest is explicitly inventoried and replayed against the production listener; these are reviewed protocol fixtures, not runtime telemetry.
boundaries.name: Official golden-wire fixtures

boundaries.contract: Every tracked cursor, JSON-RPC envelope, mirrored-header, request-state, and simulator-capture fuzz seed is explicitly inventoried. Seeds are local test fixtures and may intentionally contain malformed or exact sample values; they are never runtime logs or metrics.
boundaries.name: Protocol fuzz seed corpora

boundaries.contract: Every tracked MCP typed-schema profile fuzz seed is explicitly inventoried. These local fixtures exercise bounded compiler/evaluator behavior and are not emitted by production telemetry.
boundaries.name: Schema-profile fuzz seed corpus

boundaries.contract: Every tracked strict-JSON parse and round-trip seed used by the MCP codec is explicitly inventoried. These local fixtures may contain malformed bytes by design and are neither logs nor metrics.
boundaries.name: Shared strict-JSON fuzz corpus

boundaries.contract: Every explicit Throwable construction is inventoried conservatively as a possible application-boundary surface. This general completeness lens intentionally overlaps the request-exception and JSON-RPC error lenses. Exact exception objects and cause chains may reach documented application callbacks, while Soklet built-in fallback logging emits only bounded throwable metadata.
boundaries.name: Explicit Java Throwable construction and wrapping

boundaries.contract: Public and protected exception constructors and methods may accept or return exact messages, causes, JSON-RPC errors, request names, request values, multipart fields, and value collections. Framework-created request-exception messages are separately redacted, while typed carriers and attached cause chains deliberately preserve exact values for application handling.
boundaries.name: Exact-value exception carrier surfaces

boundaries.contract: Request-state protection factories expose only fixed failure categories and getReason() returns the finite INVALID_STATE or PROTECTOR_UNAVAILABLE enum; no protected-state bytes, authentication material, cause, or arbitrary message is retained by this carrier.
boundaries.name: Bounded request-state protection failures

boundaries.contract: The internal localization-context-unavailable carrier has only a no-argument constructor with a fixed message, disabled cause, and disabled stack trace; it cannot retain application localization data.
boundaries.name: Fixed localization-context failure

boundaries.contract: The tracked official expected-check manifest is an exact local conformance artifact. Its scenario-to-check mapping is test evidence, not a production log or metric.
boundaries.name: Official expected-check manifest

boundaries.contract: The tracked protocol-profile evidence index is captured exactly so supported-profile provenance and evidence paths remain reproducible.
boundaries.name: Official protocol-profile evidence index

boundaries.contract: The tracked official scenario manifest is exact local conformance input whose ordering and names drive the runner; it is neither emitted telemetry nor production request data.
boundaries.name: Official scenario manifest

boundaries.contract: Every tracked TraceContext fuzz seed is inventoried exactly. These local parser inputs may contain malformed or adversarial trace-header bytes by design and are not emitted by built-in logging or metrics.
boundaries.name: TraceContext fuzz seed corpus

boundaries.contract: Generic HTTP/SSE LogEvent construction can carry exact messages and other application-visible values to LifecycleObserver; it is not the restricted built-in MCP telemetry channel.
boundaries.name: Generic exact LogEvent emissions

boundaries.contract: Public MCP event factories, event getters, snapshot getters/builders, and carrier fields deliberately preserve caller-supplied or collected exact values; applications own manually created events and retained snapshots.
boundaries.name: MCP metric event and snapshot surfaces

boundaries.contract: Generic HTTP and SSE simulators and result objects deliberately preserve and render exact captured requests, responses, events, and failures for local test callers.
boundaries.name: Generic HTTP and SSE simulator capture

boundaries.contract: Unknown mirrored-header diagnostics are disabled by default and, when enabled, expose only the bounded endpoint path and sanitized header name under application/operator retention control.
boundaries.name: Opt-in mirrored-header diagnostic surface

boundaries.contract: The dedicated MCP runtime wires every internal microhttp EventLoop to NoopLogger; inventoried microhttp logger declarations and calls therefore emit no transport diagnostic for MCP traffic, and alternate wiring creates a new unclassified candidate.
boundaries.name: Disabled internal microhttp logger channel for MCP

boundaries.contract: The default generic LifecycleObserver and explicitly selected DebugLogger can write exact LogEvent messages or complete Throwable stack traces, while configuration warnings can include exact application-controlled text; applications and operators own these generic sinks.
boundaries.name: Generic direct diagnostic output

boundaries.contract: Fallback, terminal, and MCP startup direct-output paths emit only fixed, redacted, escaped, or length-bounded diagnostics and never traverse exact Throwable messages, causes, suppressed values, or stacks.
boundaries.name: Redacted and bounded direct output

boundaries.contract: The generic MetricsCollector API, default snapshots/builders, and callbacks deliberately receive or expose exact HTTP/SSE targets, addresses, requests, throwables, and event values; custom collectors own retention and export.
boundaries.name: Generic MetricsCollector exact surfaces

boundaries.contract: Generic LogEvent getters, builders, copiers, and every derived fluent attachment may carry exact messages, requests, throwables, ResourceMethod values, and MarshaledResponse values to application observers.
boundaries.name: Generic LogEvent exact-value surface

boundaries.contract: The remaining frozen artifact families intentionally preserve exact raw HTTP/query/multipart bytes, final-schema and pinned JSON Schema resources, licenses/manifests, and generic fuzz seeds for deterministic test reproduction.
boundaries.name: Additional exact conformance, schema, HTTP, and fuzz fixtures

delegations.contract: Application-created telemetry and manual metric values remain application-owned; Soklet neither sanitizes nor controls values that an application independently logs, records, exports, or retains.
delegations.name: Application telemetry and manual values

delegations.contract: Custom MetricsCollector implementations receive the documented typed event objects and own any additional dimensions, projection, export, storage, retention, and access policy.
delegations.name: Custom metric collectors

delegations.contract: Operators own log and telemetry sink configuration, access control, export, aggregation, deletion, and retention after Soklet emits its documented built-in records.
delegations.name: Operator retention and access

matcherRules.description: Every qualified or statically imported LogEvent.with(...) construction or LogEvent::with method reference in the full Soklet production source tree; the sink records the exact LogEventType token when statically named.

Every qualified or statically imported McpMetricsEvent factory invocation, every qualified factory method reference, plus every visible method, constructor, or field declaration owned by McpMetricsEvent, McpMetricsSnapshot, or their nested event/key/builder carriers; signatures, accessors, and fields make new metric dimensions fail closed.
Every LogEvent builder request(...) attachment, including copy/builder forwarding inside LogEvent itself; unrelated reactive-stream request(...) calls are excluded structurally.
Every fluent throwable(...) attachment in the declared production roots; current production uses this vocabulary exclusively for LogEvent throwable attachment and forwarding.

Exact Request/Throwable accessors and lifecycle callback invocations; every public/protected field, method, or constructor whose type/signature exposes Throwable or a frozen Request/context carrier seed; every non-rendering visible declared surface of those seeds, nested builders/copiers, and transitive implementations; and canonical constructors, carrier accessors, and implicit renderers for every record with such a component regardless of record visibility. Explicit toString overrides are represented only by the diagnostic-renderer family. Seeds include Request, trace/multipart carriers, all top-level Mcp*Context owners, localization/invocation/tool/request-id/propagation/admission/input-response carriers. Throws clauses alone are not exposure candidates.

Construction of the defined Soklet request exceptions whose payload can originate in a path, body, query parameter, form parameter, header, cookie, multipart field, or duplicate/missing value diagnostic.

Every public/protected generic HTTP/SSE and MCP simulator/result constructor or method surface, plus MCP implementation capture construction/access paths for response headers/body, stream bytes/messages, completion state, and terminal Throwables.

Every explicit production toString() declaration; canonical constructor and component accessor paths for records except the constructor and carrier-typed accessors already represented by PRIV-MATCH-005, plus an implicit renderer only when the record declares no toString override and is not already a Request/Throwable carrier rendered by PRIV-MATCH-005; and structural summary/render declarations in diagnostic, summary, and terminal-reporter owners. Signature-bearing candidates make newly added exact diagnostic values fail closed without double-classifying a concrete surface.

Every declared public/internal McpJsonRpcError or public McpJsonRpcException method, constructor, visible field, record component, construction/factory, typed accessor publication, and catch path that can place exact application messages or data on the wire; qualified constructions are included.

Every tracked regular file named by the frozen exact artifacts or below the recursive Soklet golden, official final-schema/wire, generic fuzz, and MCP schema-resource roots; a newly added artifact is an unclassified candidate and an untracked artifact fails verification.

Every explicit construction of a declared or conventional Throwable subtype, including non-suffix local subtypes discovered transitively from extends clauses, while excluding the non-Throwable DTO names JsonRpcError, McpJsonRpcError, ProtocolError, and RequestError; this general lens intentionally overlaps the request-exception and wire-error families.

Every public or protected constructor or method declaration whose selected owner is a transitively discovered Throwable subtype, including non-suffix and Error carriers; current methods expose exact values or bounded reasons, future carrier/rendering methods fail closed, and overloads retain canonical parameter signatures.

Every void emission method declared by the internal microhttp Logger abstraction, every same-vocabulary dot invocation in internal microhttp regardless of receiver expression, each no-Logger EventLoop constructor delegation keyed by its no-op/default semantics, plus every MCP-runtime EventLoop construction keyed by explicit-no-op/default-no-op/alternate semantics and every NoopLogger.instance() wiring; logger replacement therefore changes the inventory key.

Every direct System.err/System.out print, printf, println, or write call or method reference, every typed PrintStream or System-stream var-alias output call or method reference, the terminal reporter OutputStream write, and every Throwable.printStackTrace(...) call in production source.

Every visible method, constructor, or field declaration owned by the top-level MetricsCollector interface or any nested metrics carrier/builder, every visible production override of the complete top-level method vocabulary, and every dot invocation of that vocabulary across production source.

Every visible LogEvent/Builder/Copier declaration plus every invocation of the derived Builder/Copier vocabulary on qualified, statically imported, typed-receiver, or copy-chain LogEvent construction paths; new attachment names and variable-based attachments fail closed.
